name: Guru Arjan
credit: Sikh miniature portrait, 18th/19th century · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Guru Arjan (1563-1606) was the fifth of the ten Sikh Gurus, born at Goindval in the Punjab, the youngest son of Guru Ram Das. He completed the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib) at Amritsar and made the city a centre of Sikh life.

In 1604 he compiled the Adi Granth, the first form of the Sikh scripture, gathering the hymns of his predecessors with those of Hindu and Muslim saints, and adding his own, which are the largest share of the book. His Sukhmani Sahib, in Gurmukhi, is among the most widely recited Sikh compositions. He died in Mughal custody at Lahore in 1606.
